summary: Frontend E2E tests for Emergent Object Storage integration (CV upload flow + admin files panel) and new logo. All 5 requested test areas PASSED. (1) Logo: new glowing badge with wink (logo-wink-box) renders in navbar, hover triggers wink animation without console errors. (2) Client-side CV validation: setting a .txt file on lead-form-cv-input correctly rejects it — no lead-form-cv-clear button appears and toast 'Only PDF or DOC/DOCX files up to 8MB' is shown. (3) Lead form CV flow: filled contact form with valid /app/test_reports/tmp_cv.pdf, filename displayed in picker + lead-form-cv-clear visible, submit produced success toast 'Connection initialized. Our routing team will contact you within 24h.' Verified via GET /api/admin/leads that the new lead ef2d1eef-f4b9-4300-bf56-2084e3912e08 (test_cv_1787434776@ashtor.net) has cv_file_id=52913f18-8e85-4200-89e1-1d47441781e7 set. (4) Regression: submit WITHOUT CV also succeeded (lead TEST_NoCV User created, visible in admin). (5) Admin files panel: admin login successful, paperclip toggle (lead-files-toggle-{id}) opens lead-files-panel-{id}, upload via lead-file-input-{id} added a row (rows went 0→2 including CV + attachment), download button triggered a real download (suggested_filename=tmp_cv.pdf via expect_download), delete button removed a row (2→1). Hero counter and stories/landing render fine.
critical_code_review_comments: AdminTables.jsx LeadRow: after opening files panel there is a brief moment where 'No files yet' is shown before the async fetch resolves (leadFiles defaults to []). Minor UX — consider a lightweight 'Loading…' state while files are being fetched to avoid flashing the empty state.

LeadForm.jsx: after successful submit the form resets but the CV file input reference is not explicitly cleared via ref.value=''; behavior is fine because the picker is unmounted/reset via state, but re-selecting the same file after a submit could fail to fire onChange in some browsers. Consider resetting input.value.
Delete file in admin panel does not show a confirm dialog; a single click deletes irreversibly. Consider a confirm() or inline confirm state to avoid accidental deletes.
